items.title: Joe LaBarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 15, 2021
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...apparently Count Basie wouldn’t say anything unless he was really unhappy.

ctx.x: What we play as musicians, you know, we’re the most self-critical people there are. We’re listening to ourselves play and if you’re doing a recording and you’re hearing the recording played back you say to yourself, “Oh man I’ve played that idea so many times, I’ve got to get that out of my vocabulary. That’s done for now.” Things like that, you know? Or if you find an obvious flaw in what you’re doing. You’re constantly examining yourself.

Were the people you played, the leaders, would they tell you, would they give you guidance, would they like chew you out or was it sort of like, apparently Count Basie wouldn’t say anything unless he was really unhappy. So I’m just wondering, did you ever be — like look for guidance or almost welcome it and not get it? © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

I don’t know that I ever actually asked anybody, but I was fortunate in that Woody’s band, Chuck’s band — Chuck Mangione’s band, Bill Evans, and all the different sidemen— all the different leaders that I worked for in New York, they really hired you for you, so they allowed you to learn or they allowed your input. They wanted you to interpret the music the way you heard it.
